from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 6  # sources
    J = 11  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [82, 94, 106, 134, 85, 156]
    demands = [33, 53, 15, 26, 38, 23, 52, 24, 50, 31, 15]
    cost_matrix = [[16.13, 12.25, 15.61, 26.5, 13.97, 17.13, 23.56, 7.6, 10.63, 29.67, 25.83], [27.85, 20.22, 3.24, 27.9, 18.32, 4.03, 3.9, 7.75, 3.31, 4.79, 7.42], [17.34, 9.41, 3.73, 10.26, 11.54, 21.91, 27.11, 5.62, 24.68, 28.72, 8.5], [5.63, 13.93, 14.96, 7.51, 13.26, 8.33, 18.26, 25.5, 16.45, 25.9, 19.77], [7.3, 11.39, 22.1, 13.4, 6.14, 15.36, 8.7, 11.19, 23.31, 13.12, 23.82], [20.47, 26.91, 12.48, 3.84, 14.52, 20.76, 4.73, 22.83, 16.86, 13.97, 12.5]]
    emission_matrix = [[15.05, 5.51, 2.9, 9.42, 17.82, 3.61, 15.07, 6.25, 4.38, 12.4, 11.47], [1.59, 15.32, 7.76, 14.02, 8.28, 16.81, 16.13, 5.28, 9.15, 16.08, 15.22], [12.67, 10.52, 19.22, 15.01, 15.84, 14.72, 8.32, 20.0, 14.5, 1.0, 11.29], [10.63, 6.49, 13.25, 17.1, 12.51, 19.4, 13.58, 14.77, 8.21, 8.4, 6.13], [5.62, 6.17, 7.98, 9.32, 13.3, 15.81, 18.53, 3.7, 15.63, 15.78, 15.2], [10.34, 9.83, 12.51, 9.31, 18.07, 16.93, 6.27, 10.84, 3.09, 17.99, 4.82]]
    fixed_costs = [[289, 68, 268, 216, 115, 234, 54, 180, 54, 275, 240], [194, 161, 57, 224, 126, 91, 237, 179, 250, 282, 59], [90, 258, 263, 228, 225, 128, 191, 93, 100, 128, 248], [175, 175, 69, 292, 86, 134, 297, 72, 91, 216, 56], [207, 210, 230, 68, 272, 210, 167, 263, 233, 200, 208], [89, 156, 255, 123, 123, 289, 239, 84, 264, 83, 143]]
    moq = [[8, 20, 16, 16, 5, 15, 18, 13, 13, 11, 5], [17, 8, 20, 13, 14, 19, 7, 5, 7, 12, 14], [12, 17, 13, 7, 9, 12, 15, 17, 9, 10, 16], [16, 10, 8, 6, 13, 11, 8, 6, 16, 20, 6], [19, 12, 8, 13, 6, 6, 15, 19, 16, 17, 14], [12, 9, 17, 17, 15, 5, 7, 17, 5, 12, 8]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Executive Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: Today
Subject: Balanced shipping plan to manage cost and carbon

Context
Our outbound network ships product from multiple warehouses to multiple stores. Each shipping lane has both a monetary cost per unit and a carbon emission rate per unit. In practice, the lowest-dollar options often carry a higher carbon impact. We need a plan that protects margin while meeting our sustainability commitments and customer expectations, without compromising service.

Operational rules we must respect
- Route activation costs: Turning on any warehouse-to-store lane triggers a one-time setup charge (e.g., carrier onboarding, paperwork, and dock readiness). We incur this charge whenever a lane is activated, regardless of the volume moved on it. This means we should activate only the lanes that truly add value.
- Minimum order quantities on active lanes: Once a lane is active, we must move at least a defined minimum volume on it. This reflects full-truck or minimum-drop policies from carriers and avoids inefficient partial loads.
- Supplier limits per store: To manage receiving capacity and vendor complexity, each store may receive deliveries from no more than a set number of warehouses. This guardrail keeps operations practical on the ground.

Supply and demand boundaries
- Warehouse shipments cannot exceed available inventory at each origin.
- Each store’s demand must be fully met, with no underfill.
- Shipments must comply with the minimums noted above whenever a lane is used.

Management priority and evaluation approach
Leadership has set relative importance weights for cost and emissions. Cost carries somewhat more emphasis, while emissions remain a meaningful factor. We will evaluate candidate plans using a combined measure that:
- Applies the cost weight to total variable shipping cost.
- Applies the emission weight to total carbon emissions.
- Adds the one-time setup charges for all activated lanes in full (these charges are not scaled by the weights).
This approach ensures we reflect both financial performance and environmental impact while accounting for the real costs of activating lanes.

Business goal
Develop a practical shipping plan that specifies:
- Which lanes to activate.
- How much to ship on each activated lane.
The plan must meet store demand, honor warehouse supply limits, respect lane minimums, and keep the number of supplying warehouses per store within the allowed cap. Among all feasible options, we will select the one with the lowest combined score under the management-approved cost and emission weights, inclusive of setup charges.

Next steps
- Validate the data in the annex with Network Planning and Finance.
- Generate a recommended plan and a short list of near-optimal alternatives to support trade-off decisions.
- Review sensitivity to weight changes and to potential supply or demand shifts so we can adjust quickly if conditions change.
